chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said: He narrated to us al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman: Is Adhan and Iqamah obligatory upon her? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَذَانٌ: Adhan: The first call to prayer announcing the time for salat.
key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: Iqamah: The second call to prayer, recited immediately before the prayer begins.
key_terms.عَلَيْهَا: Alayha: Upon her (indicating obligation or responsibility).

ai.seo_question: Is Adhan and Iqamah obligatory for women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the reliable chain of Shaykh al-Tusi, establishes that the Adhan and Iqamah are not obligatory (wajib) for women, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these are recommended (mustahabb) acts for them rather than mandatory duties. This ruling highlights the distinction in ritual obligations between genders, where women are exempt from the communal proclamation of prayer times while still being required to perform the prayer itself.
